answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each agent to lock a copper-bonded deposit in a shared vault before it may transact: the bond is small enough for one honest agent but ruinous for a meadow of clones, since every fake identity must post its own deposit. Misbehavior triggers slashing, and the slashed funds go to the agents that reported the abuse, so running many identities costs more than it earns.
